---
title: "Typst format"
subtitle: "Tagged PDF for six document types."
description: "What mcanouil-typst gives a PDF: PDF/UA-1 tags and the veraPDF check, the page header and footer, heading numbers, cross-references, labels and dates."
---

```yaml
format: mcanouil-typst
```

`mcanouil-typst` renders all six document types to PDF, as a single document or as a Quarto book.
[This report](../preview.pdf) is rendered by the site with the format.

## Accessible PDF {#accessible-pdf}

The format sets `pdf-standard: ua-1`, so every PDF is tagged for PDF/UA-1.
Decoration is an artefact in the tags.
Logos and the ORCID badge have alternative text, and tables have tagged header cells.

Typst stops the render when the document breaks the standard:

- A heading level is skipped, for example a `###` after a `#`.
- An image has no alt text. Use `fig-alt` or a caption.
- A formula has no alt text. See the maths alt text of [typst-extras](../reference.qmd#typst-extras).

Quarto checks each PDF with veraPDF when it is installed.
To install veraPDF, run this command:

```bash
quarto install verapdf
```

If veraPDF is not installed, Quarto gives a warning and does not check the PDF.

## Header and footer

Typst pages have a header and a footer with three slots each.
Each type has its own default slots.
Covers, dividers and the first page of some types have no header, because the motif is in that corner.
See [Header and footer](../reference.qmd#header-and-footer).

## Heading numbers {#heading-numbers}

The format sets `number-sections: true`, but each type keeps its own numbering of body headings:

| Type | Body headings | Appendix sub-headings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| report, `full` layout | 1, 1.1 | A.1 |
| article | 1, 1.1 | A.1 |
| report, `compact` layout | no numbers | A.1 |
| memo, workshop, letter, invoice | no numbers | A.1 |

: How each type numbers its headings. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[36,32,32]"}

## Cross-references to sections

A reference to a numbered heading reads "Section 1".
A reference to a heading without a number reads "Section" and the heading text, for example "Section Introduction".
The word "Section" follows the document language.

```markdown
# Introduction {#sec-intro}

See @sec-intro for the context.
```

## Labels and dates {#labels-and-dates}

The labels (Exercise, Contents, Invoice and others) exist in English and French.
German has the letter labels only.
`lang` selects the language.

To change a label, write a language file and give its path in the Quarto `language` key.
Put the labels under the language code:

```{.yaml filename="my-labels.yml"}
en:
  mcanouil-exercise: "Task"
```

```yaml
lang: en
language: my-labels.yml
```

The other labels keep their values.

The format shows dates in the long form, in the order of the language:

- `lang: en` gives the United States order: "November 11, 2026".
- `lang: en-GB` gives the British order: "11 November 2026".
- `lang: fr` gives "11 novembre 2026".

## Dark PDF

`brand-mode: dark` gives a dark PDF.
See [Presets](presets.qmd#light-and-dark).
